summary: This Wikipedia article defines a sphere as the set of points in three-dimensional space at a fixed distance (radius) from a center, and covers its basic terminology, equations, and geometric properties. It gives the volume formula V = 4/3 πr³ and surface area formula A = 4πr², with Archimedes credited for the early derivations. It also discusses the sphere's role in mathematics (spherical geometry, differential geometry, topology), curves on spheres, and generalizations such as ellipsoids and n-spheres. The note is truncated before the history, gallery, and remaining sections.
one_line: Wikipedia article defining the sphere as a 3D set of points equidistant from a center, with its equations, volume, surface area and geometric properties.
key_facts: A sphere is the set of points that are all at the same distance r from a given point in three-dimensional space, called the center.
The earliest known mentions of spheres appear in the work of the ancient Greek mathematicians.
The volume of a sphere is V = 4/3 πr³, which equals π/6 d³ ≈ 0.5236·d³, where d is the diameter.
Archimedes first derived the sphere volume formula by showing the volume inside a sphere is twice the volume between the sphere and its circumscribed cylinder.
The surface area of a sphere of radius r is A = 4πr².
A sphere is uniquely determined by four points that are not coplanar.
Two spheres intersect in a circle, and the plane containing that circle is called the radical plane.
The sphere has the smallest surface area of all surfaces enclosing a given volume, and encloses the largest volume among closed surfaces with a given surface area.
In Riemannian geometry, the filling area conjecture states that the hemisphere is the optimal (least area) isometric filling of the Riemannian circle.
The sphere has constant Gaussian curvature equal to 1/r² at each point.
The antipodal quotient of the sphere is the real projective plane.
In navigation, a rhumb line or loxodrome is an arc crossing all meridians of longitude at the same angle, and loxodromes are straight lines in the Mercator projection.
Spherical geometry is a form of elliptic geometry, which together with hyperbolic geometry makes up non-Euclidean geometry.
In spherical trigonometry the sum of the interior angles of a spherical triangle always exceeds 180 degrees.
An ellipsoid is the image of a sphere under an affine transformation.

entities.name: Apollonius of Perga
entities.role: Earlier mathematician with a result for the circle that the note says the sphere's distance-ratio property follows from.

entities.name: Euclid's Elements
entities.role: Source of the traditional definition of a sphere as a surface formed by rotating a circle about its diameter.
